questions.problem:
The cubic polynomial $P(x)$ has roots ${x}_{1}=-4,$ ${x}_{2}=1,$ and ${x}_{3}=2,$ and the coefficient of the cubic term is $3.$ Find $P(x).$

$P(x)=$
{{field-1}}${x}^{3}\,+$
{{field-2}}${x}^{2}\,-$
{{field-3}}$x\,+$
{{field-4}}
questions.worked_solution:
Since our cubic polynomial has roots ${x}_{1}=-4,$ ${x}_{2}=1,$ and ${x}_{3}=2,$ and the coefficient of the cubic term is $a=3,$ we can write the polynomial as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}a(x-{x}_{1})(x-{x}_{2})(x-{x}_{3}) & =3(x-(-4))(x-1)(x-2) \\  & =3(x+4)(x-1)(x-2)\end{aligned}
$$

Expanding the parentheses, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}3(x+4)(x-1)(x-2) & =3({x}^{2}+3x-4)(x-2) \\  & =3({x}^{3}-2{x}^{2}+3{x}^{2}-6x-4x+8) \\  & =3({x}^{3}+{x}^{2}-10x+8) \\  & =3{x}^{3}+3{x}^{2}-30x+24.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $P(x)=3{x}^{3}+3{x}^{2}-30x+24.$

The cubic polynomial $P(x)$ has roots ${x}_{1}={x}_{2}=-4,{x}_{3}=1,$ and the coefficient of the cubic term is $2.$ Find $P(x).$

$P(x)=$
{{field-1}}${x}^{3}\,+$
{{field-2}}${x}^{2}\,+$
{{field-3}}$x\,-$
{{field-4}}
questions.worked_solution:
Since our cubic polynomial has roots ${x}_{1}=-4,$ ${x}_{2}=-4,$ and ${x}_{3}=1,$ and the coefficient of the cubic term is $a=2,$ we can write the polynomial as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}a(x-{x}_{1})(x-{x}_{2})(x-{x}_{3}) & =2(x-(-4))(x-(-4))(x-1) \\  & =2(x+4)(x+4)(x-1)\end{aligned}
$$

Expanding the parentheses, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}2(x+4)(x+4)(x-1) & =2({x}^{2}+8x+16)(x-1) \\  & =2({x}^{3}-{x}^{2}+8{x}^{2}-8x+16x-16) \\  & =2({x}^{3}+7{x}^{2}+8x-16) \\  & =2{x}^{3}+14{x}^{2}+16x-32.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $P(x)=2{x}^{3}+14{x}^{2}+16x-32.$

questions.problem: The cubic polynomial $P(x)$ has roots ${x}_{1}=-5,$ ${x}_{2}=0,$ and ${x}_{3}=1,$ and the coefficient of the cubic term is $-2.$ Find $P(x).$
questions.worked_solution:
Since our cubic polynomial has roots ${x}_{1}=-5,$ ${x}_{1}=0,$ and ${x}_{3}=1,$ and the coefficient of the cubic term is $a=-2,$ we can write the polynomial as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}a(x-{x}_{1})(x-{x}_{2})(x-{x}_{3}) & =-2(x-(-5))(x-0)(x-1) \\  & =-2x(x+5)(x-1)\end{aligned}
$$

Expanding the parentheses, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}-2x(x+5)(x-1) & =-2x({x}^{2}+4x-5) \\  & =-2({x}^{3}+4{x}^{2}-5x) \\  & =-2{x}^{3}-8{x}^{2}+10x.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $P(x)=-2{x}^{3}-8{x}^{2}+10x.$

questions.problem: The cubic polynomial $P(x)$ has roots ${x}_{1}=-1,$ ${x}_{2}=4,$ and ${x}_{3}=5,$ and the coefficient of the cubic term is $1.$ Find $P(x).$
questions.worked_solution:
Since our cubic polynomial has roots ${x}_{1}=-1,$ ${x}_{1}=4,$ and ${x}_{3}=5,$ and the coefficient of the cubic term is $a=1,$ we can write the polynomial as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}a(x-{x}_{1})(x-{x}_{2})(x-{x}_{3}) & =1(x-(-1))(x-4)(x-5) \\  & =(x+1)(x-4)(x-5)\end{aligned}
$$

Expanding the parentheses, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}(x+1)(x-4)(x-5) & =({x}^{2}-3x-4)(x-5) \\  & ={x}^{3}-3{x}^{2}-5{x}^{2}+15x-4x+20 \\  & ={x}^{3}-8{x}^{2}+11x+20.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $P(x)={x}^{3}-8{x}^{2}+11x+20.$

questions.problem: The cubic polynomial $P(x)$ has roots ${x}_{1}=-5,$ ${x}_{2}=-4,$ and ${x}_{3}=-3,$ and the coefficient of the cubic term is $-1.$ Find $P(x).$
questions.worked_solution:
Since our cubic polynomial has roots ${x}_{1}=-5,$ ${x}_{1}=-4,$ and ${x}_{3}=-3,$ and the coefficient of the cubic term is $a=-1,$ we can write the polynomial as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}a(x-{x}_{1})(x-{x}_{2})(x-{x}_{3}) & =-1(x-(-5))(x-(-4))(x-(-3)) \\  & =-(x+5)(x+4)(x+3)\end{aligned}
$$

Expanding the parentheses, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}-(x+5)(x+4)(x+3) & =-({x}^{2}+9x+20)(x+3) \\  & =-({x}^{3}+3{x}^{2}+9{x}^{2}+27x+20x+60) \\  & =-{x}^{3}-12{x}^{2}-47x-60.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $P(x)=-{x}^{3}-12{x}^{2}-47x-60.$

The Argand diagram above shows the roots of the cubic polynomial $f(x).$ Find $f(x)$ given that the coefficient of the cubic term is $4.$
questions.worked_solution:
From the diagram, we see that $f(x)$ has roots ${x}_{1}=0$ and ${x}_{2,3}=2\pm 2\text{i}.$ Additionally, we're given that the coefficient of the cubic term is $a=4.$ Therefore, we can write the polynomial as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x) & =a(x-{x}_{1})(x-{x}_{2})(x-{x}_{3}) \\  & =4(x-0)(x-(2+2\text{i}))(x-(2-2\text{i})) \\  & =4x(x-(2+2\text{i}))(x-(2-2\text{i}))\end{aligned}
$$

Expanding the parentheses, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}4x(x-(2+2\text{i}))(x-(2-2\text{i})) & = \\ 4x({x}^{2}-x(2-2\text{i})-x(2+2\text{i})+(2+2\text{i})(2-2\text{i})) & = \\ 4x({x}^{2}-4x+8) & = \\ 4{x}^{3}-16{x}^{2}+32x & .\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $f(x)=4{x}^{3}-16{x}^{2}+32x.$

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x) & =a(x-{x}_{1})(x-{x}_{2})(x-{x}_{3}) \\  & =-5(x-3)(x-2\text{i})(x-(-2\text{i})) \\  & =-5(x-3)(x-2\text{i})(x+2\text{i})\end{aligned}
$$

Expanding the parentheses, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}-5(x-3)(x-2\text{i})(x+2\text{i}) & = \\ -5(x-3)({x}^{2}+x(2\text{i})-x(2\text{i})-(2\text{i})^{2}) & = \\ -5(x-3)({x}^{2}+4) & = \\ -5({x}^{3}+4x-3{x}^{2}-12) & = \\ -5{x}^{3}+15{x}^{2}-20x+60.\end{aligned}

$$

Expanding the parentheses, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}(x-3)(x-(2+3\text{i}))(x-(2-3\text{i})) & = \\ (x-3)({x}^{2}-x(2-3\text{i})-x(2+3\text{i})+(2+3\text{i})(2-3\text{i})) & = \\ (x-3)({x}^{2}-4x+13) & = \\ {x}^{3}-4{x}^{2}+13x-3{x}^{2}+12x-39 & = \\ {x}^{3}-7{x}^{2}+25x-39 & .\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem: The cubic polynomial $f(x)$ has roots ${x}_{1}=3,{x}_{2,3}=\pm 5\text{i},$ and the coefficient of the cubic term is $2.$ Find $f(x).$
questions.worked_solution:
Since $f(x)$ has roots ${x}_{1}=3$ and ${x}_{2,3}=\pm 2\text{i},$ and the coefficient of the cubic term is $a=2,$ we can write the polynomial as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x) & =a(x-{x}_{1})(x-{x}_{2})(x-{x}_{3}) \\  & =2(x-3)(x-5\text{i})(x-(-5\text{i})) \\  & =2(x-3)(x-5\text{i})(x+5\text{i})\end{aligned}
$$

Expanding the parentheses, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}2(x-3)(x-5\text{i})(x+5\text{i}) & = \\ 2(x-3)({x}^{2}-(5\text{i})^{2}) & = \\ 2(x-3)({x}^{2}+25) & = \\ 2({x}^{3}-3{x}^{2}+25x-75) & = \\ 2{x}^{3}-6{x}^{2}+50x-150 & .\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $f(x)=2{x}^{3}-6{x}^{2}+50x-150.$

canonical_examples.problem: The cubic polynomial $P(x)$ has roots $x_1=x_2=2,x_3=1,$ and the coefficient of the cubic term is $3.$ Find $P(x).$
canonical_examples.worked_solution:
Since our cubic polynomial has roots ${\color{black}x_1=x_2=2}$ and ${\color{black}x_3=1},$ and the coefficient of the cubic term is ${\color{black}a=3},$ we can write the polynomial as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}a(x-{x}_{1})(x-{x}_{2})(x-{x}_{3}) & =3(x-2)(x-2)(x-1)\end{aligned}
$$

Expanding the parentheses, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}3(x-2)(x-2)(x-1) & =3({x}^{2}-4x+4)(x-1) \\  & =3({x}^{3}-{x}^{2}-4{x}^{2}+4x+4x-4) \\  & =3({x}^{3}-5{x}^{2}+8x-4) \\  & =3{x}^{3}-15{x}^{2}+24x-12.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $P(x) = 3x^3 -15x^2+24x-12.$
